description: The CLI that wires config+sources+detect+store+notify together, the uv-first docs/meta (README, Makefile, CI, config.example.toml, .env.example), the cli test, and a final full integration pass (lint+format+tests+offline demo). Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 for all imported modules and types.
steps: Create hotline/cli.py: `build_parser()` with argparse subcommands: `once` (flags --dry-run, --source repeatable with choices {web,social,audio}, --config PATH), `watch` (same flags plus --interval int default 45), `test-alert` (respects --dry-run). Handlers `cmd_once`, `cmd_watch`, `cmd_test_alert`. `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` parses args, loads config via config.load_config(args.config), selects sources (default all three), runs each source -> detect.detect on item text -> Store.should_notify dedupe -> notify.notify, printing detections. For `once --dry-run` with no reachable config/network, load the bundled fixtures/ directly (web parser over fixtures/*.html + audio windowing over fixtures/transcript.txt) so it prints detections offline with zero setup. `watch` loops with time.sleep(interval). `test-alert` sends (or dry-runs) a sample Telegram message. Return exit code 0 on success, non-zero on bad usage.

Create config.example.toml: documented, with real 987FM contest/giveaway page URLs as commented examples AND a note on using fixtures for offline runs; poll interval, user_agent, audio enabled flag + stream url, feed url. NO secrets.
Create .env.example: the four HOTLINE_ vars (HOTLINE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN, HOTLINE_CHAT_ID, HOTLINE_X_BEARER, HOTLINE_IG_TOKEN) empty with explanatory comments. No real values.

Create Makefile with uv-based targets: install (uv venv && uv sync --extra audio), test (uv run pytest), lint (uv run ruff check .), fmt (uv run ruff format .), run (uv run python -m hotline once --dry-run), lock (uv lock), clean (remove .venv, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache, *.db). Mark targets .PHONY.

Create .github/workflows/ci.yml: trigger on push and pull_request; job on ubuntu-latest; steps actions/checkout, astral-sh/setup-uv (pinned), set up Python 3.13 (uv python pin 3.13 or setup-uv python-version), `uv sync` (no audio extra), then `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run pytest`.

Create README.md: overview; uv-first setup (install uv, `uv venv`, `uv sync --extra audio` for optional audio) as the primary workflow with a short note that `pip install -e ".[audio]"` + venv also works; configuration via env + TOML; usage of all three subcommands (once/watch/test-alert); offline demo `uv run python -m hotline once --dry-run`; prominent LEGAL / ToS / ETHICS section (robots.txt respect; Mediacorp/987FM and X/Instagram scraping ToS; audio capture/transcription copyright + opt-in; rate-limit guidance: 45s default, don't hammer, back off on errors; personal/educational use); document rate limits and the polite configurable User-Agent.

Extend tests/conftest.py as needed and create tests/test_cli.py: invoke main(['once','--dry-run']) directly, assert it returns 0 and produces detections against the fixtures; assert --source web restricts sources; assert an unknown subcommand returns a non-zero exit code. No network.
If pyproject.toml dependencies changed at all during this feature, re-run `uv lock` and commit the updated uv.lock. Then run the full verification below.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run python -m hotline once --dry-run` exits 0 and prints detections from the bundled fixtures with no config or network.
`uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` are clean.
`make run` prints detections; `make test`, `make lint`, `make fmt`, `make lock` behave as described.
config.example.toml parses as valid TOML and contains no secrets; .env.example lists the four HOTLINE_ vars empty.
README documents the uv-first workflow and contains the LEGAL/ToS/ETHICS section; CI uses uv with Python 3.13.
uv.lock is present, committed, and in sync with pyproject.toml.
